Name: Wodicker, Nelson, Johnson (2024), Unified dispatch of grid-connected and islanded microgrids, Frontiers in Energy Research 11
Used for: Established outage metrics (autonomy, survivability) and the method of starting the outage at every hour of the year
Class reason: Published paper or preprint: cite, do not copy
Note: Military microgrid, diesel + battery + PV, outage started at every hour of the year over a 7-day horizon; emissions reported. No hydrogen, no campus.
What I took from it: Definitions of survivability (probability of serving 100% of critical load), autonomy (duration) and unserved energy; the all-start-times scan. Method and names are adopted, not claimed as new. Findings are not used.

Name: Lee (2026), Design-actionable cost-resilience thresholds for islanded battery-hydrogen microgrids, Int. J. Hydrogen Energy 264, 156805
Used for: Closest work to this project: hydrogen vs diesel in an outage test; basis for the difference statement and for an optional validation run
Class reason: Published paper or preprint: cite, do not copy
Note: Island microgrid (Philippines), calibrated example load; cited by 0 documents in Scopus on 30 Oct 2026. Code and data are open (GitHub, Zenodo; see the paper).
What I took from it: 8760-hour dispatch; four random outage starts per year, fixed 48 h, worst case over 10 seeds; battery-hydrogen holds 48 h while a diesel-battery system loses survivability under derating, fuel limits or start-up delay. Differences from this project: fixed duration, random starts, off-grid island, example load.

Name: Dong et al. (2018), Battery and backup generator sizing for a resilient microgrid under stochastic extreme events, IET Generation, Transmission & Distribution 12(20)

What I took from it: Critical-load coverage probability by outage start (t) and duration (d); generator and battery reliability; campus-like critical load. Method adopted, not claimed as new.
